title: Hot-path touchpoint matrix (one-page runbook)
content:
Purpose: quick cross-team matrix to surface the hot request paths (high customer impact + brittle coverage) and a lightweight owner/ETA grid for immediate triage and temporary workarounds. Use this during daily stand/scrub and pair with the longer coverage census when time permits.

Context: after last week's customer incident (JIRA-9852) we saw cascading fallback on two model routes and one routing rule. This sheet is intentionally narrow: only ‘hot’ flows that have >1x SLA breach risk in the next 72h or that are actively escalating. Not exhaustive.

Snapshot counts (2028-06-15 09:00 PT):
- routes flagged: 7
- customers affected (est): 3 enterprise + 2 mid-market pilot orgs
- observed 95/99 latency spikes during regional failover windows

Matrix (column headers: path | symptom | primary owner | backup | ETA (hrs) | mitigation | blockers / tickets | quick next action)

1) path: hosted-api/text-generate-v1 -> symptom: token-level latency spikes at 512+ | primary: Liam Ortega | backup: Eng SRE oncall | ETA: 8 | mitigation: route to quantized variant q-generate-v1-small during peak | blockers: JIRA-9852 (routing fallback), PR 4127 perf patch | next: Liam to push temporary route rule by +3h

2) path: embeddings/batch-128 -> symptom: OOMs on dedicated pools when batching burst occurs | primary: Sana Patel | backup: infra-duty | ETA: 24 | mitigation: reduce batch target to 64 and enable aggressive eviction | blockers: infra capacity claim review CONFLUENCE-38792 | next: Sana to open capacity claim & notify customers

3) path: private/proxy-connector -> symptom: auth timeouts for customers behind corporate proxies | primary: Noah Alvarez | backup: SE team | ETA: 12 | mitigation: enable extended token TTL on failing route and add retry with jitter | blockers: customer-side network trace request (pending) | next: Noah to request network trace + SE to prepare rollback plan

4) path: dedicated/burst-fallback -> symptom: burst routing not honoring burst-cap policy -> primary: Platform Eng (oncall) | backup: Platform Eng lead | ETA: 4 | mitigation: hard cap on burst for low-tier tenants | blockers: policy rollout perms | next: oncall to apply emergency cap and log effect

5) path: console/rollouts -> symptom: canary reached 10% but metrics missing for 40% of requests | primary: Product Console | backup: Observability | ETA: 6 | mitigation: pause canary, force sampling to 100% for debug | blockers: sampling flag behind feature toggle | next: Product Console to pause and Observability to collect traces

6) path: serving-runtime/kv-cache -> symptom: cache poisoning on some prompt prefixes -> primary: Serving Runtime | backup: Applied ML | ETA: 48 | mitigation: invalidate affected prefices, add short-term namespace isolation | blockers: eval on regression risk | next: Runtime to run quick regression on staging then invalidate prod namespace if green

7) path: api-gateway/edge -> symptom: occasional 503s when region fallback in-progress | primary: SRE Edge | backup: NetOps | ETA: 10 | mitigation: extend fallback window, keep warm pool in region | blockers: warm pool quota | next: SRE Edge to coordinate quota bump request with NetOps

Notes + heuristics:
- This is triage-focused. If ETA > 48h, move the row to the Coverage Backlog doc and change status to "monitor".
- If a mitigation is applied, update the matrix row with timestamp and observed impact (latency percentiles, error rate).
- Use the quick action column to capture at-most-one immediate instruction (who does what in the next 2–4h).

Quick triage checklist (for whoever owns a row):
- Confirm symptom with telemetry (top-2 relevant dashboards)
- Confirm primary owner is reachable (Slack ping + phone if >2h out-of-window)
- Push a mitigative rule (route override, cap, TTL) rather than a full change when possible
- If change is customer-impacting, CC CS and the named customer contacts in outreach

Outstanding questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enable auto-rollbacks for canaries above 5% when error rate >2x baseline? (open debate; Product/Observability)
- Short-term: grant burst-cap emergency perms to oncall for next 72h? (Platform Eng decision)

Decision log (ad-hoc):
- 2028-06-14 18:30 PT — emergency cap applied to dedicated/burst-fallback (oncall). Effect: 60% reduction in 95th p99 latency on low-tier.

Housekeeping / follow-ups (owners assign by EOD):
- Compile brief for CS customers affected (Sana)
- Add postmortem stub and link telemetry (Liam)
- Move long-duration items to Coverage Backlog doc and tag with owner (Noah)

Slack pins / quick links: CONFLUENCE-38792 (capacity claim), JIRA-9852 (incident), PR4127 (runtime perf).
